sources.citation: Blevins, Juliette. 2007. A long lost sister of Proto-Austronesian? Proto-Ongan, mother of Jarawa and Onge of the Andaman Islands. Oceanic Linguistics 46(1): 154-198 (author-posted PDF via the Internet Archive of email.eva.mpg.de/~blevins/pdf/).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.1 'Synchronic phonology' (pp. 160-162) gives Jarawa/Onge inventories, max CVC syllable, bimoraic minimal content word, four processes after Abbi 2006 -- no stress placement. Sec. 2.2 presupposes word stress without locating it: 'Jarawa e is often reduced to [schwa] in unstressed syllables' (p. 164); 'Reduction of the nonround nonhigh vowels *e and *a to schwa in unstressed syllables is variable' (p. 164); cognate-set notes refer to 'where u is stressed.. where final i is stressed' (p. 167). No rule for where stress falls.

sources.citation: Kumar, Pramod. 2012. Descriptive and typological study of Jarawa. PhD dissertation, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. xv+342 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 'Phonetics and Phonology' (pp. 36-72) is explicitly segmental ('with focus on segmental phonology', p. 36): inventory, contrasts, distribution, syllable structure V/CV/VC/CVC (2.4, p. 65), syllabification (2.5), word structure (2.6), morphophonemics (2.7). No suprasegmental/stress/accent/tone section; the string 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the thesis text layer.
